conventions.convention: S₀=I−2|0⟩⟨0|, S_good=I−2Π_good, and Q=−AS₀A*S_good. The leading minus is retained under control.

Supplied controlled-power queries and repeated controlled-Q access are distinct models. Repeated access charges every controlled constituent; an uncontrolled phase oracle supplies neither model implicitly.

The QFT amplitude estimator requires dyadic M≥4 and returns an exact real cyclotomic value. Counting additionally permits M=2 through the one-qubit QPE circuit, without invoking the M≥4 error theorem.
Counting uses N=2ⁿ with n≥0, including N=1. Raw outputs are algebraic real estimates; integer rounding is separate postprocessing.
The likelihood schedule starts at m₀=0 and uses m_k=2^(k−1) for k≥1. Every zeroth power is 1, and ties select the least grid label. No finite-sample accuracy guarantee is asserted.
Median parameters ε and δ are rational, with 0<ε≤1 and 0<δ<1; repetitions are independent and their number is odd.
Relative counting stops on a nonzero rough label or L²≥4N, uses a fresh final Count run, and rounds within 2/3. Its positive-count cost is expected; the zero-count cost retains the factor 1/ε.

load_bearing.statement: For dyadic M≥4 and integer k≥1, |ã−a|≤2πk√(a(1−a))/M+π²k²/M² with probability at least 8/π² for k=1, and strictly greater than 1−1/[2(k−1)] for k≥2. At a=0 and a=1 the outputs are exact.

Defines the finite-dimensional amplitude task, signed Grover iterate Q=−AS₀A*S_good, uniform counting specialization a=t/N, and separately declared controlled-power and repeated controlled-Q access modes.

For 0<a<1, Q restricts in ordered basis (B,G) to the rotation by 2θ, has eigenvalues exp(±2iθ), and the prepared state has squared overlap 1/2 with each normalized eigenvector. At a=0 and a=1 it has eigenvalue +1 and −1, respectively.
For M=2^m with m≥1 and eigenphase θ∈[0,1), the floor and ceiling labels of Mθ, reduced modulo M and counted once when identical, have total probability at least 8/π².

For integer s≥2 and rational polynomials P,R whose values at exp(2πi/s) are real, a terminating deterministic exact procedure decides their order or equality. No polynomial bit-operation bound is asserted.
For N=2ⁿ, n≥0, dyadic M≥4 and integer k≥1, the raw count error is at most 2πk√(t(N−t))/M+π²k²N/M² with the amplitude-estimation success probabilities. Counts zero and N are returned exactly.
For a fresh Count run with dyadic L≥2 and 0<t<N, Pr(y=0)=sin²(Lθ)/(L²sin²θ). At t=0 this probability is 1; at L=2 it is cos²θ. The label is zero exactly when the raw estimate is zero.
Given integers N≥1, even M≥2 and 0≤y<M, a terminating deterministic rational-interval procedure produces an integer q within 2/3 of N sin²(πy/M). No polynomial classical bit bound is asserted.

seams_checked.note: The phase-query definition supplies uncontrolled access only; counting explicitly requests controlled membership reflection.
Kernel, eigenspace-mixture, exact-grid, and access-cost interfaces match their uses. The counting M=2 branch uses the admissible one-qubit circuit.
The signed iterate and ordered (B,G) rotation agree, including both endpoint eigenvalues. The likelihood schedule uses uncontrolled access.
Promise, encoding, query, and classical-bit coordinates remain distinct; the relative-counting theorem explicitly states an expected-query bound.
Controlled and inverse capabilities are explicit, and the leading scalar minus is retained as a controlled relative phase.
Good/bad measurements allow zero projections; endpoint arguments avoid conditioning on zero-probability outcomes.
The nonzero finite-dimensional setting and root-to-Dirac conversion support the stated projectors and overlap calculations.
Uniform preparation uses the exact Hadamard matrix, with n ordinary gates and the empty tensor case n=0 included.
Resource accounting preserves separate controlled/inverse calls, ordinary gates, preparations, measurements, and classical work.
The dual-evaluator success proof uses the supplied rational upper bound π<22/7 faithfully.
The HHL kernel, filter, and unwrapping items use π>3 and π<22/7<16/5; these are valid consequences of the supplied bounds.

Generic relative-probability estimation uses arbitrary sampler projections, dyadic M≥4, exact comparisons, and explicitly charged controlled constituents. It does not substitute Boolean relative counting.
Indicator counting enforces M≥4 and controlled membership access. Expectation estimation retains the complete value-rotated preparation, independent medians, and access-mode-specific costs.
The finite-grid subgradient and spectral-minimum-shift items use the rational π bounds without strengthening them.
